issues.body: `no_change_census` strips the attempt suffix (`run_id.split(".", 1)[0]`) and counts every matching health record, while `_orchestration_lane_runs` counts the workflow-run object once and returns only its base `id`. The model-health ledger deliberately retains separately executed outcomes such as `123.1` and `123.2` for a full rerun under the same GitHub run id. Both records therefore enter `worker_no_change_1h`, but the Actions list contributes only one `worker_attempts_1h`. This violates the documented `no_change <= attempts` invariant, permits a published rate above 1, and can falsely sustain `worker-no-change`. The test only proves that one suffixed record matches; it does not cover two attempts of one run id.
issues.fix_hint: Define numerator and denominator over the same attempt-level population. Carry an exact attempt identity through collection and match the full ledger `run_id`, or enumerate/count concluded attempts if historical attempts are intended to count. Account for recorder-only reruns that preserve the producing attempt. Add a non-vacuous test with at least two retained attempt records sharing one base run id and assert both the intended count and that the rate cannot exceed 1.
issues.title: Rerun attempts can make the no-change numerator exceed its denominator

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The new census is not bounded to the population used as its denominator. A rerun keeps the same GitHub workflow-run id while producing a distinct model-health record keyed by the attempt suffix, so multiple retained no-change outcomes can be joined to one run counted once. This can publish rates above 1 and generate false alerts. The added tests exercise an attempt suffix but omit the multiple-attempt case that breaks the stated invariant.
